To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) spatial representation is critical for AU detection, (2) CNNs can reduce person-specific biases, and (3) temporal modeling can be achieved by stacking LSTMs on top of CNNs, and that (4) the proposed network is able to learn AU models, and that (5) the proposed network can improve the performance of AU detection

1) CNNs can be used to learn spatial representations that are robust to person-specific biases; 2) LSTMs can be used to model temporal dependencies regardless of the input video lengths; 3) a hybrid network architecture that jointly models spatial and temporal cues can achieve superior performance compared to state-of-the-art; and 4) learned models reveal how machines see facial expressions.

(i) CNNs are able to reduce person- and expression-specific biases caused by traditional hand-crafted descriptors; (ii) LSTMs are able to capture temporal dependencies of AU activations, which are not modeled by CNNs; (iii) our proposed hybrid network architecture is able to jointly model spatial and temporal cues, which are not addressed by existing studies.
